page.overview:
What is Thunderbird?

The Thunderbird was a large, magical avian beast native to North America, and most commonly found in Arizona in the southwestern United States. A close relative of the phoenix,

The Thunderbird was described as having a head that was "similar to that of an eagle"; or, in the wizarding world, "similar to that of a Hippogriff". They possessed three pairs of powerful wings, and had feathers that shimmered with cloud-like patterns.

Thunderbirds, much like their phoenix cousins, were very intelligent. It's unknown if they had a language of their own like phoenixes did, but Thunderbirds were capable of understanding human speech and could respond to simple 'yes' or 'no' questions.

Thunderbirds could create rain storms in their wake as they flew. They were known to change colours as they summoned storms, with their iridescent feathers shifting from various shades of gold to electrifying blue, to grey and silver, to white, and even to deep navy. Under normal circumstances, they caused rain to bring life to the deserts they called home. However, Thunderbirds could also sense danger, so they could also make storms when they were in distress, possibly as a way to either warn friends or to handle the crisis itself. It was unlikely that one could understand a particular Thunderbird's situation once it returned to the ground and the storm subsided. To understand properly, one would need to actually fly up into the eye of the generated storm with a Shield Charm up and confront the Thunderbird while it was still agitated.
